review_candidates.title: SVP, Chief Operating Officer
review_candidates.description: United Power is seeking an accomplished and forward-looking electric utility executive with the breadth to lead Operations, Engineering, and Safety in a complex and changing environment. The ideal candidate will bring senior-level responsibility for multiple operational or technical functions and demonstrated success overseeing system reliability and resiliency, safety performance, emergency response, infrastructure and capital priorities, and applicable NERC Reliability Standards and CIP requirements. This leader will be able to translate strategy into measurable results, strengthen compliance and accountability, develop senior leaders, and guide significant cross-functional initiatives involving technology, regulatory compliance, system capacity, and large-load interconnections. Experience in a union environment and an electric cooperative or public power organization is highly valued. Equally important, the successful candidate will be a collaborative, credible, and engaging leader who communicates effectively with employees, the ELT, the Board of Directors, regulators, members, and external partners and inspires a culture of safety, inclusion, continuous improvement, and service to members. The Position The Senior Vice President and Chief Operating Officer (COO) works under the general direction of the President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO). In collaboration with the CEO & Executive Leadership Team (ELT), the COO is responsible for the long-term transformational efforts for the utility’s Operations, Engineering, and Safety departments, and for implementing the overall strategy and direction for the organization. The COO leads strategic initiatives including, but not limited to, infrastructure construction, maintenance and upgrades, system reliability and resiliency; employee and public safety; regulatory compliance; and process and technology improvements while maintaining operational excellence. This position manages the overall Operations, Engineering, and Safety teams and their budgets, including promoting cross-functional collaboration, continuous process improvement, operational efficiencies, cost control, and a strong organizational safety culture. The COO is responsible for legal compliance with applicable operational, technical, safety reliability, security requirements, and regulatory standards, specifically, applicable North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Standards including Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP). This position reports directly to the CEO and is a member of the ELT. Essential Job Functions: Serves as a member of the ELT; participates in the formulation of strategies, company cultural norms, objectives, and policies for recommendation and dynamic presentations to the Board of Directors. Identifies a clear, motivating, and challenging vision for the Operations, Engineering, and Safety departments, with a focus on creating an aligned culture. Consistently demonstrates the ability to align team and department goals with company goals and achieve measurable results. Inspires a shared direction and encourages staff to question past assumptions and challenge the status quo. Conceives and leads implementation of the long-term transformational efforts in collaboration with the CEO, ELT, the Cooperatives Energy Risk Management Committee (ERMC) and Board of Directors. Develops and implements plans for the operational infrastructure of systems, processes, and personnel designed to maintain efficient operations. Provides strategic oversight of field and control center Operations, Engineering, and Safety programs supporting employee and public safety, system reliability, resiliency, capacity, regulatory compliance, and long-term infrastructure needs. Prepares the annual work plans and budgets for the Operations, Safety, and Engineering departments and makes recommendations to the CEO. Aligns all functional departments to operate together and with the larger organization, seamlessly and effectively to achieve goals and overall strategy. Directs the preparation of short-term and long-range operational, engineering, and safety plans and budgets; collaborates with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) on annual operating and capital budgets and oversees the prioritization, budget performance, resource allocation, and delivery of related programs and initiatives. Manages the financial aspects of the Operations, Engineering, and Safety departments with a focus on fiscal responsibility and cost-consciousness in accordance with applicable policies. Provides executive oversight of compliance with applicable federal, state, local, and industry operational, engineering, safety, reliability, and security requirements, including applicable NERC Reliability Standards and CIP requirements. Ensures appropriate accountability, governance, monitoring, documentation, reporting, training, internal controls, and corrective-action processes are established and maintained within assigned areas of responsibility. Provides executive sponsorship and oversight of the organization’s NERC compliance program within assigned operational and technical areas, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate resources, effective controls, timely reporting, cross-organizational coordination and accountability for compliance obligations. Maintains executive awareness of applicable and emerging NERC Reliability Standards and CIP requirements; evaluates organizational impacts and ensures required operational, technical, procedural, training, documentation, and system changes are implemented. Reviews significant NERC compliance risks, potential violations, audit or assessment findings, mitigation plans, and corrective actions; and ensures matters with material regulatory, reliability, cybersecurity, financial, or reputational implications are promptly elevated to the CEO and other appropriate stakeholders. Supports NERC registrations, audits, certifications, self-assessments, investigations, compliance monitoring, and regulatory reporting by ensuring assigned departments maintain complete, accurate, timely, and defensible records and evidence. Actively participates in the Energy Risk Management Committee (ERMC) and provides operational, engineering, safety, reliability, and compliance expertise to support enterprise risk evaluation and decision-making. Provides executive leadership, sponsorship, or subject-matter support for large-load interconnection initiatives and other significant cross-functional projects, as assigned. Establishes measurable goals and key performance indicators for Operations, Safety, and Engineering; evaluates performance, trends, and risks through operational and financial data and implements corrective actions as needed. Advises the CEO and the Board on Operations, Safety, and Engineering issues and strategies. Partners with Human Resources on the direction and administration of labor relations strategies. Identifies industry trends and participates in external groups to implement best practices in distribution, including advances in technology. Promotes safe, reliable, and high-quality execution within Operations, Safety, and Engineering and reinforces continuous improvement and accountability. Follows up on specific service complaints and outages; takes necessary action to maintain continuity and reliability of service as needed. Ensures the maintenance programs (i.e., tree trimming, pole line inspection, pole changeouts, OH/UG line patrol, substation inspection, etc.) are prioritized and functional. Ensures coordination between departments, including Systems Operations, Operations, Communications, and Member Services, is effective during outages and emergencies. Provides executive leadership for emergency preparedness, outage response, service restoration, and operational continuity; ensures plans are current, coordinated across departments, and regularly communicated and exercised. Provides executive leadership and oversight of the Safety Department, including organizational safety strategy, safety programs, regulatory compliance, employee training, incident prevention, emergency preparedness, performance measurement, and continuous improvement. Promotes a proactive and accountable safety culture throughout the organization by integrating safety considerations into operational planning, engineering, construction, maintenance, emergency response, resource allocation, and executive decision-making. Reviews significant safety incidents, trends, hazards, compliance concerns, and organizational risks; ensures appropriate investigations, root-cause analyses, corrective actions, and preventive measures are completed and communicated. Leads, develops, and holds accountable the Operations, Safety, and Engineering leadership teams; builds organizational capability, supports succession planning, and ensures appropriate workforce and resource planning. Creates, expands, and maintains professional and productive working relationships with peers and stakeholders. Works collaboratively with colleagues and fosters a spirit of cooperation and inclusion in the workplace. Performs other such duties as may be requested or assigned to fulfill the needs of United Power in the interest of good management practice. Minimum Qualifications: A bachelor’s degree in business administration, engineering, construction management, or a related field is required, along with a minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible leadership experience in electric utility operations, engineering, safety, reliability, or a closely related function. Experience must include executive- or senior-level responsibility for multiple operational or functional areas. Candidates must also have demonstrated experience overseeing compliance with applicable NERC Reliability Standards and providing leadership or oversight for electric utility safety, regulatory compliance, incident prevention, investigations, corrective actions, and organizational safety performance. An equivalent combination of education and substantial directly related experience may be considered in lieu of the degree requirement. Must have a valid Colorado driver’s license or the ability to obtain one. In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a generous benefits package that includes an employee retirement plan, 401K with match, paid holidays, vacation & sick leave, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability, long-term disability, and life insurance. For a full list of benefits, please visit our careers page at https://www.unitedpower.com/careers. Additional information about this recruitment can be found here: https://www.unitedpower.com/sites/default/files/Careers/COO_Brochure_UnitedPower_2026.pdf United Power is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. United Power prohibits discrimination against applicants or employees on the basis of age 40 and over, race, gender identity, sex, sexual orientation, color, religion, military or veteran status, national origin, disability, genetic information or any other applicable status protected by state or local law. We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, this position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. NOTE: This position description is not intended to be all-inclusive; an employee will also perform other job responsibilities as assigned by the immediate supervisor or management. Management reserves the right to change position descriptions, specifications or work schedules to accommodate individuals with disabilities or as the need arises.

The Position The Administrative and Procurement Associate post is located in the UNFPA Eastern Europe and Central Asia Regional Office (EECARO) in Istanbul. The incumbent will be part of the operations team and will work under the direct supervision of the Regional International Operations Manager (RIOM). The incumbent takes a client- oriented, results-focused approach to interpreting the rules, procedures and guidelines, and provides support and guidance to the region serving as a regional center of excellence. The incumbent will play a key role in supporting the RIOM in developing and implementing regional and cluster focused operational initiatives to achieve operational efficiency and effectiveness, while playing a pivotal role in providing expert guidance to the RO and CO operations personnel on procurement and administrative policies and procedures. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies. In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff, who embody these international norms and standards, and who will defend them courageously and with full conviction. UNFPA is seeking candidates that transform, inspire and deliver high impact and sustained results; we need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them and who commit to deliver excellence in programme results. Audit Follow-up in the region: Act as a resource to the region in addressing, leading, and assisting the RIOM in implementing internal and external audit recommendations related to procurement, administration, and affiliate workforce management to ensure high accountability and proper risk management. Procurement and Contract Lifecycle Management Procurement Strategy and Planning: Assist the RIOM in the strategic management of procurement by acting as the overall coordinator for the Regional Office's procurement processes, from requirement definition to contract closure. Ensure mandatory clearances are secured from SCMU and relevant HQ for solicitations over $100,000. Submit documents to UNDP LCRC, HQ CRC, and other review committees to obtain the correct procurement authority approval before awarding. Oversight and Closure: Manage the complete, up-to-date log of all Contracts, POs, and LTAs, ensuring timely renewal and proper contract closure. Provide technical advice to Country Offices identifying opportunities for pooling resources / consolidation within the region. Planning and Compliance: Lead the preparation and submission of quarterly affiliate workforce recruitment plans and monitor implementation. Facilitate and coordinate all formal and informal hiring processes, ensuring compliance with relevant UNFPA Policies. Tax and Fraud Control: Share the VAT tax exemption card with vendors and maintain a log and control over its use to reduce the risk of fraud and abuse of privileges. Coordinate initiatives on procurement harmonization , and streamline the use of LTAs established by other UN agencies (piggybacking) in compliance with UNFPA procedures. Administration, Logistics, and Process Improvement Logistical Support: Support the RIOM in the administrative portfolio by managing logistical support, drivers’ schedules/dispatch , and ensuring timely renewal of premises-related service contracts. Vehicle Management: Assist RIOM with vehicle management, ensuring compliance with UNFPA policy, maintaining accurate records (registration, insurance) , validating logs, overseeing driver costs, and ensuring scheduled maintenance. SOPs and Reporting: Assist the RIOM in developing, updating, and preparing SOPs, analysis, and reports for related processes, suggesting improvements to maximize efficiency. Education Qualifications and Experience: Completed Secondary Level Education required. First level university degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration or similar discipline is desirable. Knowledge And Experience Minimum of seven (7) years of relevant experience in administration, procurement and logistics, premises and services management. Proven experience and track record in successfully managing and implementing procurements and administrative functions, processes and systems in development organizations at national or international level. Expert knowledge of policies and procedures related to the public sector supply chain management, administration, affiliate workforce management, and other relevant operational policies and procedures is required. Expertise in the specific United Nations policies and procedures are preferred. Proficiency in current Microsoft Office applications (especially Microsoft Excel and Word). Experience in using Oracle based ERP system or similar cloud based ERP systems. Ability to identify, gather and generate analytical reports and interpret them for management and operational decision making. Ability to write clearly and concisely. Working experience with UN organizations is desirable. Languages Fluency in English and Turkish is required.
